late_public_findings.observation: Materialized permission data is anchored to a ZedToken revision. The recommended consumer stores computed permission data, stream cursor and revision transactionally; restart resumes from the stored cursor/revision, and batched consumers advance the durable revision only after the final batch. Snapshot-to-watch handoff starts watching from the stored snapshot revision to avoid gaps.
late_public_findings.boundary: This is durable replication/recovery provenance. It does not authorize an unrelated external effect at the stored revision.

late_public_findings.observation: Authzed recommends storing the returned ZedToken alongside protected resource content and explicitly points to Zanzibar ContentChangeCheck as the content-change pattern. The safe interpretation is a causal binding between newly written content and the authorization snapshot used for that content change.
late_public_findings.boundary: The checked public evidence does not show an external content-storage API atomically consuming the prior authorization revision as its mutation precondition, so this remains distinct from PRIOR_AUTH_REVISION_EFFECT_GATE.

late_public_findings.observation: The merge-request approval endpoint accepts sha and returns 409 when it does not match the current MR HEAD. Merge-train admission likewise accepts sha and requires it to match source HEAD. GitLab approval settings can remove approvals when commits are added, with patch identity used for reset decisions.
late_public_findings.boundary: Head-SHA binding proves content identity continuity for the approval/effect chain; it does not by itself prove all current project/rule requirements are satisfied.

independent_axes: authorization-state revision provenance and causal content binding
effect-state exact precondition and request-local authorization
refined_model.rule: Do not collapse any one axis into another. A prior allow, policy/model ID, decision ID, approval object, object etag/resourceVersion, content SHA, or idempotency key is authoritative only for the provider semantics explicitly attached to that token.
refined_model.true_external_gate_status: No real public PRIOR_AUTH_REVISION_EFFECT_GATE was proven in this fresh revision-7 evidence set. The strongest near-miss is causal authorization-to-content epoch binding; the strongest observed effect boundary remains request-local authorization composed with state CAS.

acceptance_and_counterexamples: A ZedToken that can replay an authorization read is not enough to authorize a later unrelated write.

A content record stored together with the authorization revision that justified that content change is a stronger causal binding, but is still not an external effect-server atomic revision gate unless the effect API consumes the token.
Materialized permission data + cursor without committing the corresponding revision in the same transaction is incomplete restart evidence.
GitLab approval with an omitted/stale head SHA must not be treated as the same-content approval primitive; the SHA-bound form is the fail-closed form.
A merge-train/merge request head-SHA precondition does not substitute for current approval/rules evaluation.
An idempotency key solves ambiguous repetition, not authorization freshness or target-state equality.

new_fixture_coverage: negative case where different approval/effect content identifiers do not qualify as same-content CAS
